hints: At a point of contact, the curves have both the same value and the same gradient at \(x=p\).
Use \(\cos p=k/(1+p)\), then differentiate both curve equations and equate their derivatives at \(p\).
Eliminate \(k\) between the value and gradient equations, then divide by \(\cos p\) to obtain the required relation in \(p\).
walkthrough:
State the equations of the two curves:
$$y_1 = \cos x, \quad y_2 = \dfrac{k}{1 + x} = k(1 + x)^{-1}$$

Differentiate both functions with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{dy_1}{dx} = -\sin x$$
$$\dfrac{dy_2}{dx} = -k(1 + x)^{-2} = -\dfrac{k}{(1 + x)^2}$$

Since the two curves touch at $x = p$, they share the same $y$-value at $x = p$:
$$\cos p = \dfrac{k}{1 + p} \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Since the curves touch, they also share the same gradient (tangent slope) at $x = p$:
$$-\sin p = -\dfrac{k}{(1 + p)^2} \implies \sin p = \dfrac{k}{(1 + p)^2} \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 2 by Equation 1 to eliminate the constant $k$:
$$\dfrac{\sin p}{\cos p} = \dfrac{\dfrac{k}{(1 + p)^2}}{\dfrac{k}{1 + p}}$$

Simplify both sides of the equation:
$$\tan p = \dfrac{k}{(1 + p)^2} \times \dfrac{1 + p}{k} = \dfrac{1}{1 + p}$$

State the final concluded identity:
$$\tan p = \dfrac{1}{1 + p}, \quad \text{as required.}$$

ai_rubric.Forming Equations for Numerical Solution: Differentiating $y=x\cos x$ and $y=k/(1+x)$ at $x=p$ and eliminating $k$ gives $\tan p=\frac1{1+p}$.

hints: Use the given fixed-point recurrence in radian mode, beginning with a sensible estimate for \(p\) in \([0,\pi/2]\).
Substitute each current value into \(p_{n+1}=\tan^{-1}(1/(1+p_n))\) and record every iterate to 5 decimal places.
Continue until successive iterates agree sufficiently to justify one stable value when rounded to 3 decimal places.
walkthrough:
State the given iterative formula in radian mode:
$$p_{n+1} = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + p_n}\right)$$

Compute successive iterations, giving each value to $5$ decimal places:
$$p_2 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 0.5}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) \approx 0.58800$$
$$p_3 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 0.58800}\right) \approx 0.56199$$
$$p_4 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 0.56199}\right) \approx 0.56946$$
$$p_5 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 0.56946}\right) \approx 0.56730$$
$$p_6 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 0.56730}\right) \approx 0.56792$$
$$p_7 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + 0.56792}\right) \approx 0.56774$$

Confirm the value of $p$ correct to $3$ decimal places using a sign-change check on the continuous function $f(x) = \tan x - \dfrac{1}{1 + x}$ on the interval $[0.5675, 0.5685]$:
$$f(0.5675) = \tan(0.5675) - \dfrac{1}{1 + 0.5675} \approx 0.63737 - 0.63796 = -0.00051 < 0$$
$$f(0.5685) = \tan(0.5685) - \dfrac{1}{1 + 0.5685} \approx 0.63886 - 0.63755 = +0.00130 > 0$$
Since there is a sign change and $f(x)$ is continuous on $[0.5675, 0.5685]$, the root $p$ lies in this interval.

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Applies the iterative formula by direct substitution. Concludes with \(p=0.568\). The final result is \(p=0.568\).

skill_tags: Using a Numerical Result in a Model

hints: Return to the equality of the two curve values at their contact point: \(\cos p=k/(1+p)\).
Rearrange this equation for \(k\), then substitute the iterated value of \(p\) from part (b) without premature rounding.
Evaluate in radian mode and round the resulting constant to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Recall Equation 1 from part (a):
$$\cos p = \dfrac{k}{1 + p}$$

Rearrange to make $k$ the subject:
$$k = (1 + p)\cos p$$

Substitute the converged value $p \approx 0.56778$ (or $0.568$):
$$k = (1 + 0.56778)\cos(0.56778\text{ rad})$$
$$1 + p \approx 1.56778$$
$$\cos(0.56778) \approx 0.843098$$
